title: Obscure certainty: divine faith, then moral human faith that excludes rash doubt
source_text: IV. Certitudo Obscura est earum rerum quas sola fide, vel opinione tenemus. Cujus certitudinis primum gradum habent quae propter divinam authoritatem certo creduntur. Et haec est certitudo fidei divinae, estque simpliciter & absolute certitudo, quoniam nulla ratione potest ei subesse falsum. Secundum gradum obscurae certitudinis habent ea quae creduntur ob authoritatem humanam, sed ita confirmatam & celebrem, ut omnem prorsus formidinem excludat. Qualia sunt Ciceronem & Virgilium fuisse insignes viros, Augustum magnae parti Orbis terrarum feliciter imperasse, multas esse civitates praeclaras in provinciis a nobis longe dissitis, Constantinopolim in Thracia, Goam in India, Mexico in America. Atque haec dicitur certitudo fidei humanae, sive certitudo moralis. Quae tametsi non tanta sit, ut ei nullo modo falsum subesse possit (si quidem omnis homo mendax), tamen tanta est, ut temerarius merito judicetur, qui contra sentiat, aut disputet.
pass_a_gloss: Obscure certainty is of those things which we hold by faith alone or by opinion. The first degree of this certainty belongs to those things which are certainly believed because of divine authority. And this is the certainty of divine faith, and it is simply and absolutely certainty, because in no way can falsehood underlie it. The second degree of obscure certainty belongs to those things believed because of human authority, yet so confirmed and celebrated that it excludes fear altogether—as that Cicero and Virgil were distinguished men, that Augustus successfully ruled a great part of the world, that there are famous cities in provinces far from us, Constantinople in Thrace, Goa in India, Mexico in America. And this is called the certainty of human faith, or moral certainty. Which, although it is not so great that falsehood can in no way underlie it (since every man is a liar), yet is so great that he is rightly judged rash who thinks or disputes the contrary.
pass_b_english: Obscure certainty begins with divine faith, to which no falsehood can attach.
Next is moral or human-faith certainty—like believing famous cities exist—strong enough that contrary doubt is rash, though not absolutely infallible.

choices.why: Technical Roman grade below divine faith.
